predecessors.name: Tibetan Empire
predecessors.text: Karasahr (Yanqi) and Kucha, 'taking them from the Tibetan Empire'

successors.name: Chagatai Khanate
successors.text: the Qocho land as corrected for 1126-1138 (Turfan, Beshbalik, Karashahr; Hami; without Gansu, Kucha and Aksu)

ledger.x: 843: the Uyghurs under Pangtele take Karasahr and Kucha from Tibet.
866: Pugu Jun, first idiqut, takes the Turfan basin and Beshbalik.
904: the Guiyi Circuit occupies Hami and Gaochang.
By 1096: Qocho loses Kucha and Aksu to the Kara-Khanids.
1128: Qocho becomes a Qara Khitai vassal and goes on.
1335: the infobox ends the Mongol vassalage ('Vassal state of the Mongol Empire (1209-1335)').
1370: the vassalage ends with the kingdom (bridge).

wars.name: Qocho conquest of the Guiyi Circuit's Xizhou and Tingzhou
wars.outcome: Qocho took Gaochang, Beshbalik, Changbaliq and Luntai in 866 and Hami in 876; attacks on the Guiyi Circuit were repelled in 869-870 and Shazhou in 880.

wars.name: Guiyi occupation of Hami and Gaochang
wars.outcome: Zhang Chengfeng of the Guiyi Circuit seized Yizhou and Xizhou in 904; the occupation ended after the Ganzhou Uyghurs defeated the Jinshan Kingdom in 911.

wars.name: Kara-Khanid conquest of Kucha and Aksu
wars.outcome: By 1096 Qocho had lost Aksu, Tumshuk and Kucha to the Kara-Khanid Khanate.

certainty.note: Oasis cities of the Tarim's northern rim and the Turfan basin with the Tianshan steppe; Cliopatria holds one shape for 280 years and no page gives a frontier.
Vassal centuries (Qara Khitai, Mongols, Chagatai): the kingdom kept its idiqut, no page gives a frontier or an extent, and the shape is the 1126 one carried forward.
